conventions: The verbless לוּלֵי clause 'If it had not been Jehovah who was on our side' (vv.1–2) divides as: לוּלֵי → discontinuous 'If … not' (rule 25); the cleft 'it' is its own added unit (rule 20's verbless-cleft sentence); the construction-supplied copula 'had been' joins the name as the clause's anchor (rule 20); the written שֶׁ takes 'who'; הָיָה takes 'was'; the dative לְ takes 'on … side' headed on 'side' (rule 24) with 'our' on the suffix (rule 18). The competing reading — the whole 'If it had not been' as the particle's fixed formula under rule 30 — was named in the notes and not taken.
report: Checked all eight candidate lemmas; none is a split. הוּא (Sp1cp) varies only by the pronoun case the ASV writes (our/us); בְּ, לְ and עַל vary by the English relation the ASV chose per context; יהוה carries 'had been' in vv.1–2 because it is the anchor of the verbless לוּלֵי clause and is bare in v.6 (subject of 'Blessed be') and 'of Jehovah' in v.8 (rectum) — each licensed by the source.

Recurring constructions are consistent across verses: לוּלֵי → 'If … not' with cleft 'it' added and the copula on the name (vv.1, 2, per rule 20's verbless-cleft sentence); לָנוּ → 'on … side' on the preposition with 'our' on the suffix (vv.1, 2); temporal בְּ + infinitive → 'When' (vv.2, 3); phrasal particles 'rose up', 'swallowed … up' kept with their verbs (vv.2, 3); 'had gone over our soul' identical in vv.4 and 5.

Articles: v.1 rectum article unrepresented because the ASV writes 'A Song of Ascents' with no 'the'; v.5 agreement article on זֵידוֹנִים unrepresented under rule 47; v.4/v.7 'the' to the written article. Construct פַּח in v.7 takes a supplied 'the' and the anarthrous participle rectum takes 'of the fowlers' under rules 19 and 46; v.8 constructs likewise.
BSB disagreements (PSA.124.4 directive he on נַחְלָה; PSA.124.5 agreement article) are both documented convention differences — the ASV writes nothing for either — and neither is an error.
No patches. One convention recorded for the לוּלֵי formula so PSA.124's division is findable. No promotions or amendments: nothing here is new to the contract.
